module_title: Selling at Markets, Events, and Online

lessons.title: Setting up a stall at local markets and fairs
lessons.body:
Start by visiting your local market or fair to see what sells and where you can fit in. Talk to the market master or organiser about stall fees. In many African markets, a daily stall fee ranges from 500 to 2,000 shillings (or equivalent) depending on location and day. For a first try, book a smaller stall or share with another vendor to keep costs low. Choose a spot with foot trafficânear entrances, food areas, or busy walkways. Avoid corners where people pass quickly.

Your stall must look clean and inviting. Use a simple table covered with a bright, clean cloth. Display your ginger and turmeric shots in clear bottles or small cups so customers see the golden colour. Put up a hand-painted sign with big letters: âGINGER SHOTS â BOOST YOUR IMMUNITYâ and prices. Have a small cooler or bucket with ice to keep shots cold. For teas, bring a thermos with hot water and sample cups. Keep a waste bin for used cups.

Price clearly. For example, sell a 100ml shot for 1,000 shillings or 3 for 2,500. Offer a small discount for bulk orders. Prepare a simple menu board listing: Ginger Shot, Turmeric Shot, Ginger-Turmeric Mix, and Hot Ginger Tea. Train yourself to greet every person who passes: âHello! Try our fresh ginger shot â it fights colds and gives energy.â Smile and make eye contact.

Pack enough stock: for a busy market day, bring at least 50 shots and 100 tea servings. Keep a notebook to record sales and popular items. Bring change in small notes and coins. At the end of the day, count your money, subtract stall fees and transport, and note your profit. Repeat at different markets to find your best location.

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp and social media to take orders
lessons.body:
WhatsApp is the easiest tool to start selling online. Create a WhatsApp Business account (free) and set your profile name to something clear like âAminaâs Ginger Shots â Nairobiâ. Add a profile photo of your product and a status message: âFresh ginger & turmeric shots delivered. Order now!â Save your customersâ numbers and label them (e.g., âCustomer â Westlandsâ).

Post daily status updates showing your shots being made, packed, or delivered. Use short videos: pour the shot, show the ginger root, or a happy customer drinking. Include prices and how to order: âSend a message to 0712 345 678. Delivery in Nairobi for 200 shillings.â In your status, you can also ask questions: âWhich flavour do you prefer â ginger or turmeric?â This gets replies and keeps you visible.

For orders, use a simple system. When someone messages, reply quickly: âHello! Thanks for your interest. We have 100ml shots at 1,000 each or 3 for 2,500. Where are you located?â Confirm the order, total price, and delivery time. Ask for payment via M-Pesa or mobile money before delivery, or cash on delivery for regular customers. Keep a list of orders in a notebook: name, number, items, amount, location, and time. This helps you avoid mistakes.

Also use Facebook Marketplace and Instagram if you have data. Post clear photos with prices and your WhatsApp number. Join local community groups on Facebook and WhatsApp (e.g., âNairobi Buy & Sellâ) and post your offer once a week. Do not spam; instead, offer a free sample to the group admin. For deliveries, use boda boda or a friend with a motorbike. Charge a small delivery fee (e.g., 200â500 shillings) or offer free delivery for orders above 5,000 shillings. Always ask customers to refer friendsâgive them 10% off their next order if they do.

lessons.title: Partnering with health shops and gyms
lessons.body:
Health shops and gyms are goldmines for repeat customers. Walk in during quiet hours (mid-morning or early afternoon) and ask to speak to the owner or manager. Dress neatly and carry a small cooler with free samples. Introduce yourself: âHello, I make fresh ginger and turmeric shots. Iâd like to supply your shop/gym. Can I leave a few samples for you and your customers to try?â

Offer a simple wholesale deal. For example, you sell a 100ml shot to them at 700 shillings, and they sell it at 1,200. For a gym, suggest a commission: they display your shots at the counter, and you give them 20% of each sale. Or they buy at wholesale and keep the profit. Provide a small branded fridge or cooler with your logo and price list. Agree on a delivery scheduleâtwice a week, for instance, on Monday and Thursday mornings.

For health shops, highlight the health benefits: ginger reduces inflammation, turmeric is good for joints, and both boost immunity. Bring a one-page flyer with ingredients, no preservatives, and your contact. Offer to do a free tasting session on a Saturday morning. Many shops will agree if you handle the setup and cleanup. During the tasting, give out small cups and collect phone numbers for your WhatsApp list.

For gyms, target personal trainers and fitness instructors. Offer them a free shot after their workout. Ask them to recommend your product to clients. You can also sponsor a small gym eventâprovide 50 free shots in exchange for your banner being displayed. Keep records of each partner: name, contact, order size, delivery days, and payment terms. Follow up with a thank-you message after each delivery. If a partner sells well, offer them a bonus (e.g., one free pack for every 10 sold). This builds loyalty and steady income.

lessons.title: Offering free samples to attract new customers
lessons.body:
Free samples are the fastest way to turn a stranger into a buyer. People are more likely to buy after they taste. Plan your sampling session carefully. Choose a busy location: outside a market, near a gym, at a church event, or during a sports match. Get permission from the venue owner or local authority. Prepare small cups (30â50ml) and fill them just before the event to keep them fresh. Keep them in a cooler with ice.

Make your sample station attractive. Use a small table with a bright cloth, a sign that says âFREE TASTE â GINGER & TURMERIC SHOTSâ, and a tip jar or price list nearby. As people pass, smile and say: âWould you like to try a free energy shot? Itâs good for immunity.â Hand them a cup and watch their reaction. If they like it, immediately offer to sell a full bottle: âThat was a sample. A full 100ml bottle is 1,000 shillings, or 3 for 2,500. Would you like one?â

Keep track of how many samples you give and how many sales you make. For example, if you give 100 samples and sell 30 bottles, thatâs a 30% conversion rateâvery good. If sales are low, try a different location or time. Always collect phone numbers: âCan I add you to my WhatsApp list for weekly specials?â Offer a small incentive: âIf you buy now, Iâll give you a free sample for a friend.â

Do not give unlimited free samples to the same person. Limit to one per person. Also, target people who look like they care about healthârunners, gym-goers, mothers with children. Avoid giving samples to small children without asking a parent. After the event, send a WhatsApp message to everyone who gave their number: âThanks for trying our shot! Hereâs a 10% discount on your first order. Reply YES to order.â This turns a one-time taster into a regular customer.

lessons.title: Handling cash and mobile money payments
lessons.body:
You must be able to accept both cash and mobile money. In most African countries, M-Pesa, Airtel Money, MTN Mobile Money, or Orange Money are common. Register for a merchant account if possible, or use your personal number. Display your mobile money number clearly on your stall and on your WhatsApp status. For cash, always carry small notes and coins for change. Never keep all your money in one pocketâuse a money belt or a small locked box under the table.

When a customer pays by mobile money, ask them to show you the confirmation message before you hand over the product. Check the amount and the recipient number. If you have a smartphone, you will get an SMS or notification. Do not rely on a customerâs screenshot aloneâit can be faked. For large orders, wait for the money to reflect in your account. If you are unsure, call your mobile money providerâs customer care to confirm.

For cash payments, count the money in front of the customer. Say the amount: âYou gave me 5,000. Your total is 3,000. Here is your 2,000 change.â This avoids disputes. Keep a small notebook to record every sale: date, time, items sold, amount, payment method (cash or mobile money), and customer name or number. At the end of the day, balance your cash and mobile money totals against your notebook. If there is a difference, find out why.

Security is important. Do not display large amounts of cash. If you are at a market, make friends with nearby vendors and watch each otherâs stalls. For mobile money, set a PIN that is hard to guess and never share it. If you accept payments online, use a separate phone or SIM for business. Always thank the customer and give them a receipt (a handwritten note is fine). This builds trust and makes them more likely to return.

lessons.title: Keeping simple sales records in a notebook
lessons.body:
A notebook is your most important business tool. Buy a hardcover exercise book and a pen. On the first page, write your business name, your name, and the date you started. Then create columns for each day: Date, Item, Quantity, Unit Price, Total, Payment Method, Customer Name/Number, and Notes. For example: â12/06/2025, Ginger Shot 100ml, 5, 1,000, 5,000, M-Pesa, Mary 0712..., delivered.â

At the end of each day, total your sales. Add up all the Totals. Then subtract your expenses for that day: transport, market fees, ingredients, packaging, and any helperâs pay. Write the profit at the bottom. For example, if you sold 5,000 and spent 1,500, your profit is 3,500. Do this every day, even if you are tired. It takes only 5 minutes and shows you if you are making money or losing it.

Every week, review your notebook. Which product sells most? Which market or day is best? Who are your repeat customers? Use this to plan: buy more ginger if shots sell fast, or try a new location if sales are low. Also track your debts: if a customer promises to pay later, write it down and follow up. If you buy ingredients on credit, record that too.

Keep your notebook safeâdo not leave it at the stall. At the end of the month, add up all profits. Compare with previous months to see growth. If you want a loan or to partner with a shop, your notebook is proof that you are a serious business. You can also use a simple phone app like âM-Pesa statementâ or âExcelâ if you have a smartphone, but a notebook works even without electricity or data. Always write in pen, not pencil, so records cannot be erased.

quiz.q: What is a reasonable daily stall fee at a local market in many African cities?
quiz.explanation: Stall fees vary, but 500â2,000 shillings is typical for a small market stall.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good way to display your shots at a market stall?
options: A) In a closed cardboard box
B) In clear bottles or small cups on a bright cloth
quiz.explanation: Clear display shows the product's colour and makes it inviting.

quiz.q: Why should you bring a cooler with ice to your stall?
options: A) To keep shots cold and fresh
quiz.explanation: Cold shots taste better and stay safe to drink.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end of a market day?
options: A) Count money, subtract costs, note profit
B) Give away leftover shots for free
C) Leave your stall without cleaning
quiz.explanation: Recording sales and costs helps you know if you made a profit.

quiz.q: What is a good greeting to attract customers to your stall?
options: B) 'Hello! Try our fresh ginger shot â it fights colds and gives energy.'
quiz.explanation: A friendly greeting with a benefit gets attention.

quiz.q: Which app is easiest to start selling online in Africa?
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp Business is free, widely used, and simple for orders.

quiz.q: What should you include in your WhatsApp status to get orders?
options: B) Short videos of your product, prices, and how to order
quiz.explanation: Product videos and clear ordering instructions drive sales.

quiz.q: When taking orders on WhatsApp, what should you confirm with the customer?
options: B) Order items, total price, and delivery time
quiz.explanation: Confirming details prevents mistakes and builds trust.

quiz.q: What is a good way to get more orders from existing customers?
options: B) Offer 10% off if they refer a friend
quiz.explanation: Referral discounts encourage word-of-mouth marketing.

quiz.q: Which social media platform is good for posting product photos with prices?
quiz.explanation: Facebook Marketplace is widely used for local buying and selling.

quiz.q: What is a good wholesale price to offer a health shop if you sell retail at 1,200?
quiz.explanation: Wholesale should be lower so the shop can profit.

quiz.q: How can you motivate a gym to partner with you?
options: A) Offer them 20% commission on each sale
B) Demand they buy 1000 bottles upfront
quiz.explanation: Commission gives the gym an incentive to sell your product.

quiz.q: What should you bring when approaching a health shop?
options: A) Free samples and a one-page flyer
quiz.explanation: Samples let them taste, and a flyer explains benefits.

quiz.q: Why is a free tasting session good for a health shop?
options: A) It attracts customers and collects phone numbers
quiz.explanation: Tastings create interest and build a contact list.

quiz.q: What should you do after delivering to a partner?
quiz.explanation: A thank-you maintains a good relationship.

quiz.q: What is a good size for a free sample cup?
quiz.explanation: Small samples are enough for a taste without wasting product.

quiz.q: Where is a good place to offer free samples?
options: A) Outside a gym or at a busy market
D) In a school exam room
quiz.explanation: High-traffic health-conscious locations work best.

quiz.q: What should you say when handing a sample?
options: A) 'Would you like to try a free energy shot? Itâs good for immunity.'
quiz.explanation: A friendly invitation with a benefit encourages trial.

quiz.q: If you give 100 samples and sell 30 bottles, what is your conversion rate?
quiz.explanation: 30 sales out of 100 samples is 30%.

quiz.q: What should you do after a sampling event?
options: A) Send a WhatsApp message with a discount to those who gave numbers
quiz.explanation: Follow-up turns tasters into paying customers.

quiz.q: Which mobile money service is common in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa is widely used in Kenya and parts of East Africa.

quiz.q: When a customer pays by mobile money, what should you do before handing over the product?
quiz.explanation: Always verify the payment in your own account or SMS.

quiz.q: Why should you count cash in front of the customer?
options: A) To avoid disputes over change
quiz.explanation: Counting together ensures both agree on the amount.

quiz.q: What should you record in your sales notebook?
options: A) Date, item, quantity, price, payment method
quiz.explanation: These details help you track sales and profit.

quiz.q: How often should you balance your cash and mobile money?
options: A) At the end of each day
quiz.explanation: Daily balancing catches mistakes early.

quiz.q: What is a security tip for handling cash at a market?
options: A) Do not display large amounts of cash
B) Keep money in an open basket
C) Tell everyone how much you have
quiz.explanation: Keeping cash hidden reduces theft risk.

quiz.q: What should you write on the first page of your sales notebook?
options: A) Business name, your name, start date
quiz.explanation: This identifies the notebook as your official record.

quiz.q: What does profit equal?
quiz.explanation: Profit is what remains after subtracting costs.

quiz.q: Why should you review your notebook weekly?
options: A) To see what sells best and plan
quiz.explanation: Weekly review helps you make better business decisions.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of keeping good sales records?
options: A) You can get a loan or partnership
quiz.explanation: Records prove your business is serious and creditworthy.
